Plasma Glucose Range Required for Admission/Dosing
data.description: Admission to CRU can be rescheduled if plasma glucose is outside the required range on Day 1
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Hypoglycemia Induction Target (Insulin Infusion Stop)
data.description: Trigger for stopping insulin infusion and proceeding to study treatment administration
data.text: Insulin infusion is stopped once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL; approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Edinburgh Scale During Hypoglycemia Induction
data.description: Timing condition for administering Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale during induction
data.text: During hypoglycemia induction will be when PG ≤75 mg/dL.

data.name: Interim Safety Review Condition for Continued Dosing
data.description: Dosing of remaining patients is contingent on safety review of first 6 patients after completion of Period 2 Day 1
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients (regardless of type of diabetes) are administered LY900018 in Period 2, and the remaining patients will be dosed after confirmation of the safety. The investigator and Lilly CRP or scientist will review available safety data, including AEs, SAEs, vital signs, ECGs, and safety laboratory tests, from these patients after they complete Period 2 Day 1. If no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure are noted, the remaining patients will be dosed.

data.name: Insulin Regimen Acceptability
data.description: Review of insulin regimen required before hypoglycemia induction procedure
data.text: Review patients' insulin regimens to confirm acceptability to undergo the procedure to induce hypoglycemia.

data.name: Insufficient Response to Glucagon
data.description: Condition triggering rescue procedures following glucagon administration
data.text: Procedures for Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration (Section 9.2.4).

data.name: Treatment-Emergent ADA Follow-up Condition
data.description: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED require additional immunogenicity follow-up until titer resolution or 1 year
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up. Samples for immunogenicity should be collected every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline (ie, returns to within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Non-inferiority Decision Criterion
data.description: Primary analysis success criterion
data.text: Non-inferiority of LY900018 will be declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI constructed on the difference in percentage (IMG - LY900018) is less than the NIM of 10%.

data.name: Patient Replacement Condition
data.description: Condition under which discontinued patients may be replaced
data.text: If patients discontinue from the study before completion of both periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason, the patient may be replaced. Replacement should not occur beyond 75 patients enrolled, if it is expected to have at least 66 patients complete the study.

data.name: PG Stability Before Meal/Discharge
data.description: Investigator must confirm plasma glucose stability prior to meal/discharge; prandial insulin may be given
data.text: After completion of all PK sampling, patients will be provided a carbohydrate-rich meal. The investigator will ensure the patient's PG is stable. A prandial insulin dose will be administered if needed.

data.name: Extended Inpatient Stay Condition
data.description: Patient may remain inpatient beyond the minimum 6 hours at investigator discretion
data.text: Patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration. A patient may remain inpatient at the CRU at the discretion of the investigator. Patients may stay longer as needed, at the discretion of the investigator.

data.name: Period 2 Timing Consistency
data.description: Procedural time-of-day consistency condition between periods
data.text: Procedures in Period 2 will occur at approximately the same time as those in Period 1.

data.name: Screening to Period 1 Transition (Randomization)
data.text: Patients will undergo a screening examination within 28 days prior to enrollment. Prior to the study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1, patients will be randomly assigned to a treatment sequence (either LY900018 in Period 1 and IMG in Period 2, or vice versa).

data.name: Period 1 to Washout Transition
data.text: Patients will be administered a single dose in Periods 1 and 2, which will be separated by a washout period of 3 to 14 days.

data.name: Washout to Period 2 Transition (Crossover)
data.text: After the 3 to 14 day washout, patients cross over to the alternate treatment (LY900018 or IMG) according to the randomized treatment sequence. Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Period 2 to Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients will return for a follow-up visit 26 to 30 days (within 28±2 days) after the last study treatment.

data.name: Follow-up to Additional TE ADA Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up with immunogenicity samples every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Dosing Hold Pending Interim Safety Review
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients are administered LY900018 in Period 2; the remaining patients will be dosed only after confirmation of safety (no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure).

data.name: Rescue for Insufficient Response to Glucagon
data.text: Procedures for insufficient response to glucagon administration will be followed (Section 9.2.4); bedside PG monitoring for safety is performed during induction and up to 120 minutes post study treatment.

data.name: Discontinuation of Inadvertently Enrolled Patients
data.text: If the sponsor or investigator identifies a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria and was inadvertently enrolled, a discussion must occur between the Lilly CP/CRP and the investigator to determine if the patient may continue in the study. Continuation requires documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP.

data.name: Discontinuation from the Study - Concurrent Research Enrollment
data.text: Patients will be discontinued for enrollment in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or enrollment in any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

data.name: Discontinuation for Medical/Safety/Regulatory Reasons
data.text: Participation in the study needs to be stopped for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and good clinical practice.

data.name: Discontinuation by Investigator Decision
data.text: The investigator decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study for any reason. If this decision is made because of an AE, SAE, or a severe hypoglycemia event, appropriate measures are to be taken. Lilly or its designee is to be alerted.

data.name: Discontinuation by Patient Decision
data.text: The patient, or legal representative, requests to be withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Study Termination for Safety
data.text: Following the review of the safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1, the study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the Investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Early Discontinuation with Required Follow-up
data.description: Patients discontinuing from the study prematurely for any reason must complete AE and follow-up procedures as shown in the Schedule of Activities, including the Follow-up/ED visit within 28±2 days after last study treatment.

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of both treatment periods with an evaluable primary outcome and the follow-up visit 26 to 30 days (28±2 days) after the last study treatment; patients with TE ADA complete additional immunogenicity follow-up until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: A patient will be considered lost to follow-up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site, after diligent contact attempts by site personnel.

data.name: Study Discontinuation by Sponsor/Investigator
data.description: The study will be stopped following review of the safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1 if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the Investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Exit of Inadvertently Enrolled Patient
data.description: A patient who did not meet enrollment criteria and was inadvertently enrolled will be discontinued unless documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP is obtained to continue with or without continued treatment.

data.name: Randomization to Treatment Sequence
data.description: Prior to study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1, patients are randomly assigned to a treatment sequence (LY900018 then IMG, or IMG then LY900018).

data.name: Admission Eligibility Decision (Plasma Glucose Check)
data.description: Admission to CRU can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop / Dosing Decision
data.description: Once bedside PG reaches <60 mg/dL the insulin infusion is stopped and approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Interim Safety Review Decision (First 6 Patients)
data.description: After the first 6 patients complete Period 2 Day 1, the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist review safety data to decide whether remaining patients may be dosed or the study stopped.

data.name: Discharge Decision
data.description: Patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration once PG is stable and the carbohydrate-rich meal has been provided; may remain inpatient at investigator discretion.

data.name: TE ADA Additional Follow-up Decision
data.description: At Follow-up/ED, patients with treatment-emergent antidrug antibodies enter additional follow-up with samples every 84±7 days until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Rescue Decision for Insufficient Glucagon Response
data.description: Based on bedside PG monitoring post glucagon administration, rescue procedures for insufficient response are initiated.

data.name: Primary Non-inferiority Analysis Decision
data.description: Primary analysis comparing treatment success rates in 66 completers; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 2-sided 95% CI of difference is <10%.
